input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Idle and stale resource reports in the web console

## Description

This epic delivers per-project idle and stale resource reporting in the RHOAI
web console, giving cluster administrators visibility into reclaimable
capacity. The console gains a report surface showing, per project, workbenches
that have been idle (with their last activity, owner, and reserved resources)
and pipeline runs that are stale (completed runs older than a configurable age
that still retain artifacts). Both reports can be exported as CSV.

The report data is sourced from existing platform telemetry: the notebook
controller's per-workbench activity tracking and Kubeflow Pipelines run
completion metadata. No changes are made to the notebook controller or to
Kubeflow Pipelines — both keep working as-is and serve as read-only data
sources.

## Scope

- A per-project idle-workbench report in the web console listing each
  workbench's last activity timestamp, owner, and reserved resources, sourced
  from the notebook controller's activity tracking.
- A per-project stale pipeline-run report listing completed runs older than a
  configurable age that retain artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run
  metadata.
- A configurable age threshold for the stale pipeline-run report.
- CSV export of either report.
- Read-only reporting only: no automated or UI-initiated reclamation,
  deletion, or culling actions, and no cost/chargeback calculations (strategy
  out of scope).
- Screenshots or caption updates elsewhere in the console that fall out of
  this change are updated as part of the same change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing activity, when an
  administrator opens the idle-workbench report, then each workbench is listed
  with its last activity timestamp, owner, and reserved resources, and the
  values match the notebook controller's activity tracking for that
  workbench.
- Given a project containing completed pipeline runs of differing ages, when
  an administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report with a given age
  threshold, then only completed runs older than the threshold that retain
  artifacts are listed, and the entries match Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Given the stale pipeline-run report, when an administrator changes the
  configurable age threshold, then the report contents update accordingly.
- Given either report, when an administrator exports it as CSV, then the
  resulting file contains the report rows and columns as displayed.
- Given the reports, when reviewed, then no reclamation, deletion, or cost
  calculation actions are offered — the feature is informational only.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner,
  reserved resources) sourced from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking.
- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
  configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines
  run metadata.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): CSV export of either report — shares the same report
  surfaces and data-fetch code as HLR-1/HLR-2, so it is delivered within this
  epic rather than as a separately schedulable deliverable.

# Documenting the idle and stale resource reports and safe reclamation

## Description

This epic delivers user documentation for the console's idle and stale
resource reporting capability once it ships: what each report shows, where to
find it, how the configurable age threshold works, how to export reports as
CSV, and the safe steps an administrator should follow to reclaim capacity
from an idle workbench or a stale pipeline run (including the caveat that
reclamation is a manual, deliberate act — the feature itself only reports).

## Scope

Content outline:

- A documentation topic introducing idle and stale resource reporting: the
  problem it solves for administrators and where the reports live in the web
  console.
- Reference documentation for the idle-workbench report: the columns (last
  activity, owner, reserved resources), the data source (notebook controller
  activity tracking), and how to interpret idle state.
- Reference documentation for the stale pipeline-run report: the configurable
  age threshold, retained artifacts, and the Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata
  source.
- A how-to section covering CSV export of either report.
- A how-to section on safe reclamation steps for idle workbenches and stale
  pipeline runs, making explicit that the reports are informational and
  reclamation/deletion is manual and out of the feature's scope.
- Cross-links from existing workbench and pipelines documentation to the new
  reporting topics where a reader would look for them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the shipped reports, when a reader opens the documentation, then the
  report descriptions (columns, data sources, configurable threshold, CSV
  export) match the implemented behavior in the web console.
- Given an administrator following the documented reclamation steps, when the
  steps are executed against a test project, then they are accurate and
  complete for both idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs.
- The documentation has been technically reviewed against the implemented
  reports by the team that built them, and review feedback is addressed.
- The documentation states that the reports are informational only and that
  automated reclamation and cost calculations are not part of the capability.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9016: Idle resource reporting in the web console

## Triage Analysis

Step 0 Check 1 (below-threshold) was evaluated and rejected on the
multiple-distinct-work-streams escape condition. The strategy has a single
active component (the web console) and effectively a single code team, and no
open questions — but HLR-4 asks for new documentation topics explaining the
reports and safe reclamation steps, which is substantive content authoring, a
distinct work stream from the console code (different skills, different review
criteria, different PR review cycles). Incidental doc touch-ups this is not.
The strategy therefore gets a full decomposition. Check 2 (documentation only)
does not apply: the web console requires code changes.

## Component Graph

Canonical component mapping (from `.context/rhai-components.txt`):

| Strategy component | Canonical component | Owner team | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| RHOAI web console | Dashboard | RHOAI Dashboard | Active (code changes) |
| Notebook controller | Notebooks | Workbenches | Passive (data source, no code changes) |
| Kubeflow Pipelines | Data Science Pipelines | RHOAI Pipelines | Passive (data source, no code changes) |

Mapping notes: "RHOAI web console" → `Dashboard`, "Notebook controller" →
`Notebooks`, "Kubeflow Pipelines" → `Data Science Pipelines` — closest
canonical names, all present in the canonical list.

Passive components: the strategy states the notebook controller already tracks
last-activity timestamps and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion
metadata — "the data exists; it is just not surfaced". No code changes are
required in either passive component, and no other team is assigned to
validate them (no Impacted Teams table exists; no such assignment anywhere in
the strategy). Validation that the reports faithfully reflect the notebook
controller's activity tracking and the KFP run metadata therefore becomes
acceptance criteria on the Dashboard epic, per the passive-component rule. All
three components exist in `.context/architecture-context/`
(`dashboard.md`, `notebooks.md`, `data-science-pipelines.md`), so no new
component onboarding chain and no component-existence Investigation is needed.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Idle and stale resource reports in the web console | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 | Documenting the idle and stale resource reports and safe reclamation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Docs | P2 |

```mermaid

    E001[RHAISTRAT-9016-E001: Idle and stale resource reports]
    E002[RHAISTRAT-9016-E002: Documentation]
    E001 --> E002
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring always last) | Documentation describes the reports that were built; it must reflect the shipped behavior, fields, and configuration. No other Implementation epics exist. |

No other edges: only one code epic exists (single component, single team, one
logical change — a per-project idle/stale resource report surface in the
console), so there are no implementation-to-implementation boundaries to draw.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources) sourced from notebook-controller activity tracking. |

| HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | **bundled**: CSV export of either report is a presentation capability on the same report surfaces and the same data-fetch code as HLR-1/HLR-2 — it shares the UI surfaces and data structures of the P1 work and has no standalone surface of its own, so splitting it out would create a second epic building the same views. The P2 label reads as relative value, not a deferral signal. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 | Substantive documentation authoring — distinct work stream, separate epic. |

Full coverage: HLR-1 through HLR-4 all map to at least one epic; no orphaned
requirements. Priority inheritance: E001 is P1 (highest priority of the HLRs it

## Epic Boundary Analysis

The two reports (idle workbenches, stale pipeline runs) are kept in a single

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing.
